on_failure.block: --on-failure block: every tool call these hooks match (__MATCHERS__) is refused on a machine where a bundle file is missing or __PYTHON__ is older than Python 3.11 (the hook exits 2, on any client version), and, on Claude Code 2.1.295 or later, where __PYTHON__ is missing or cannot start, or the hook crashes or times out.
on_failure.allow: --on-failure allow: every tool call these hooks match (__MATCHERS__) goes ahead unchecked on a machine where __PYTHON__ is missing, older than Python 3.11 or cannot start, or a bundle file is missing, and whenever the hook crashes or times out; the note is the hook's own stderr, or Claude Code's hook-error notice when the interpreter cannot start.

requirements: Every machine needs Python 3.11 or later at __PYTHON__ exactly: the hook commands start that file directly (exec form, no shell), so neither PATH, git config nor a shell picks the interpreter.
onFailure needs Claude Code 2.1.295 or later (client_versions); an older client lets a crashed or timed-out hook through.
Monitor commands are checked only on Claude Code 2.1.314 or later, and WebSocket watches never (client_versions, not_covered).
The bundle must sit at deploy_root exactly: the hook commands name it by absolute path.

The bundle folder and __PYTHON__ must be owned by an administrator and not writable by users: whoever can write them can replace the guard. The vendor docs state no ownership rule for the files a managed hook runs; on who can change the managed source they say "a developer who is an administrator on the machine can edit the managed source itself".
caveats: Managed settings bind Claude Code only. A local administrator can edit or delete these files.
On WSL, /etc/claude-code is writable by the user as well.
By default (managedSourcesBehavior "first-wins") a machine that also receives server-managed or MDM policy skips the managed settings files without a warning; /status names the source in use.
onFailure has no effect on Stop hooks, so the turn-end gate lets the turn end when it cannot run, whatever --on-failure says.

A repository holding .chock/stop.json (valid or not) makes these hooks refuse every tool call they match while Claude Code works in that repository: the bundled runtime honours chock's repository stop.

Files under the user's home folder can also stop these hooks: ~/.chock/stops/_everywhere.json (chock stop --everywhere) refuses every tool call they match, in every repository; the other files there refuse calls in their repository; an unreadable ~/.chock/stops refuses every call. The user can create these files, and so can the agent with any tool these hooks do not match (stop_files).
The bundled runtime runs git from PATH for repository facts (the stop files, the turn-end gate's changed files); the guards' verdicts on a command do not depend on it.
Hooks write their decision log under the user's home folder (~/.chock/log).
A file in managed-settings.d that is not valid JSON stops Claude Code from starting.
The labels are vendor-docs evidence, unwitnessed, best-effort: nobody has watched this file refuse a call yet.
claude_code.lock_note: --lock adds allowManagedHooksOnly. The vendor docs list what it changes on the machine: only managed hooks, Agent SDK hooks and hooks of plugins the managed settings force-enable run; user, project and local hooks, hooks and mods of other installed plugins (chock's own project hooks and plugins included) and hooks in agent frontmatter are blocked; monitors of other plugins do not start; plugins with a command source are disabled and marketplace headersHelper commands are blocked unless disableCommandPluginSources is set to false; the status line and file suggestion are read from managed settings only; the /goal command cannot run.
claude_code.never_note: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly is never emitted: it would discard every user and project permission rule.

client_versions.needed_for: onFailure (--on-failure block refuses a call when the hook cannot start, crashes or times out)
client_versions.quote: Requires Claude Code v2.1.295 or later

client_versions.needed_for: the Bash|PowerShell matcher also checking commands Claude starts with the Monitor tool
client_versions.quote: A `PreToolUse` or `PermissionRequest` hook with a `Bash` matcher also runs on shell commands Claude starts with the Monitor tool. Requires Claude Code v2.1.314 or later.

not_covered: Monitor commands on a client older than 2.1.314: the hook never sees them.
WebSocket watches started with the Monitor tool, on every client version (vendor docs, read 2026-11-13: "A hook with a `Bash` matcher doesn't run for a WebSocket watch").
MCP tools and any other tool that no emitted matcher names (the shell matcher is Bash|PowerShell), even when it runs a command.

stop_files.path: .chock/stop.json in any repository the call works in or names
stop_files.effect: every tool call these hooks match is refused; a stop file that is not valid JSON refuses as well.
every tool call these hooks match is refused, whatever the repository or session; any content, {} included, counts.
tool calls that work in or name that repository are refused, and so is every call while Claude Code names no project folder.
if it exists but cannot be listed, or an entry in it cannot be read, every tool call these hooks match is refused.
